title: Choose the world for the second POC
question: A fresh, all-ages design world for Daylight — built from scratch, nothing inherited from the coupon book. The roll assigned Almanac. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. You can pick more than one to be built.

options.label: Almanac
options.lineage: the newspaper weather page, its key, and the tide table
options.thesis: The family's day read as a forecast: conditions reported, never praised.
options.viewport: A slate masthead with today's headline, then the daylight band — sun-up to sun-down with each obligation pinned at its hour — then a permanent four-symbol key, then the day as an almanac table of time, symbol, title and owner.
options.risk: A key is one more thing to learn, and the band needs a density rule before a packed 4-to-6pm turns to mush.

raised.raise: Unowned is drawn as hatching on the band and in the table, so an empty slot is a texture you see before you read a word.
Every state is a word as well as a colour, so the screen survives greyscale and a colour-blind parent.

options.label: Primer
options.lineage: mid-century picture-book graphic programs — Bruna, Golden Books
options.thesis: Five flat inks and one thick line: the proven system for a four-year-old and an adult reading the same page.
options.viewport: A cobalt header, then the family as a row of person-tokens with an empty dashed token for 'no one', then outlined cards each carrying its owner's token, a state word and full-width answer buttons.
options.risk: Also where most attempts at a kid-legible product land, and it tips childish the moment the forms get rounder or cuter — the discipline is holding it flat and adult.

options.label: Departures
options.lineage: public transport signage programs — platform signs, not the board hardware
options.thesis: A family week is departures and arrivals; every one has a time, a destination and a named driver.
options.viewport: A dark shell, the next unanswered departure as a lead panel with its status plate and elapsed time, then today as a four-column table — time, what, who, state mark.
options.risk: A board for a schedule is the clever default in this category, and the dark shell is the harder read for a young child in daylight.

options.label: Roster
options.lineage: the school gym's painted roster wall
options.thesis: Every obligation is a plate with a name on it, and reassigning is physically moving the plate.
options.viewport: A painted header, a filter row, then the family as vertical columns — a dashed 'No one' column first — with each item a plate slotted under its owner.
options.risk: Sport framing can read competitive, which this product's voice forbids; it must carry no score, no streak, no ranking at all.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a family organiser ships — executed better than any of them do it.
canonCard.viewport: White ground, segmented control, rounded status cards with avatar owners and 44pt answer buttons, five-tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
